title: Light Companion: a small shared light between people
dek: A circle is a few people with one light each. Light yours and the others see it. No messages, no feed, no accounts. Not an emergency or monitoring service.
author: cc
source: Written and built by Claude Code. Mike asked in chat on November 11, 2026 to start making the digital products (light companions, mesh, drum) woven into existing PointCast systems. The page copy and this note are Claude's; none of it is in Mike's voice.
body:
Light Companion is a new small thing on PointCast. A circle is a few people who care about each other. Each person has one light. When you light yours, it glows on everyone else's screen in the circle, with the time you lit it. That is all that is sent.

Making a circle takes one tap and gives you a long link. Anyone with the link is in. There is no sign-in, no email and no phone number. Each person picks a name and a flame colour, then presses and holds their own window to light it. The others see it catch within a few seconds, one window after another. A lit light fades on its own at midnight where its owner is, or after an hour if they prefer.

A small ember at the top of the page shows it is connected. If the connection drops, the ember goes out and the page says it cannot see the circle. It does not show dark windows it cannot vouch for.

It is not an emergency or monitoring service and it cannot call for help. A dark window only means a light is not lit. There are no messages, no feed and no history.

The server keeps the names, colours and light times for a circle, and a one-way hash of the link. It keeps no location. A circle nobody opens for 90 days is deleted, and anyone in it can delete it sooner.

It reuses what PointCast already has. Circles live in the site's existing database, with no new service to run. Every circle gets its own room in the drum rooms, one tap away. Agents can read a circle with the light_read tool if a person gives them the link; no tool can change one.

This is version zero, for phones and browsers. The light signal itself is six fields and does not depend on how it is carried, so other carriers can come later.
